data.text: Hello! Another update about FungWong (it will be named Uwan in the Philippines). To Besties in the affected areas, please prepare. This system is forecasted to bring heavy rainfall, so flooding is possible. Stay safe and keep monitoring official weather updates.

quoted_tweet.text:
HEADS UP! ⚠️🌀⛈️

Those in the Northern Luzon and Central Luzon should take precautionary measures in anticipation to the Tropical Storm #FungWong that will enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) tomorrow evening, November 7 as a typhoon (#UwanPH).

Based on the latest assessment from the global models and the weather agencies, the center (future eye) of TS Fung-wong could make landfall between Cagayan-Isabela-Aurora area in the early hours of November 10, 2025 (Monday) as a super typhoon. 💨🍃

HOWEVER, despite that the storm will directly hit the above-mentioned areas, the outer rainbands of TS Fung-wong could possibly affect the Bicol Region and Eastern Visayas by early Sunday, November 9 due to its huge circulation, with a diameter of more than 1,000 kilometers.

Deterioration of the weather conditions should therefore arrive in the Northern and Central Luzon by mid-Sunday, with potential life-threatening rainfall and gusty winds by Monday (November 10) and Tuesday, November 11.

Wind Signal No. 5 is the highest possible warning for the areas that will be directly affected by the storm, with more than 200 mm+ or TORRENTIAL amount of rainfall in many areas in Luzon.

Catastrophic flash floods, landslides and storm surges are likely, particularly in the hazard-prone areas. ⚠️

Be alert and prepared. Please continue monitor the official updates, advisories and bulletins from the DOST-PAGASA (@dost_pagasa) and your respective local government units (LGUs).

data.text:
International Weather Update  The Philippines Hit Hard by Typhoon Kalmaegi (TinoPH) 🌪️

Good morning everyone,

While we’ve been dodging the Cornish drizzle, over in the Philippines it’s a very different story. The big clean-up is now underway across parts of Cebu City, after powerful Typhoon Kalmaegi (locally named TinoPH) tore through the region, bringing howling winds, torrential rain, and devastating flooding.

Homes have been left caked in thick layers of mud, as shown in the video below. It’s hard to believe the sheer amount of silt and debris the storm left behind. Roads have turned into rivers, and many families are now working tirelessly to clear what’s left and start rebuilding their lives.

Kalmaegi is the latest in a series of storms to hit the western Pacific this season, reminding us how quickly tropical weather can turn destructive. The Philippines experiences around 20 typhoons a year, but even for a country well-prepared for storms, this one hit hard.

The local authorities and volunteers are out in full force helping communities recover, and thankfully, emergency response teams were quick to act saving many lives despite the destruction.

Our thoughts are with everyone affected by this powerful storm. ❤️

We’ll continue to share updates from the region as more information comes in.

Kind regards,
KWT Dave
